construct: Performance at reproducing selected AI research papers under a fixed long-horizon agent, compute, time, and grading setup.
unit_of_analysis: One agent attempt to reproduce the central experimental contribution of one selected paper.
interaction_type: Long-horizon tool-using agent operating in an isolated research-compute environment.
target_outcome: Paper-specific rubric score over produced code, artifacts, and experimental results.
human_participants: No human subjects. Paper authors and ML experts contribute rubrics, clarifications, validation, and human baselines.
elicitation: The agent receives the paper, task materials, a scaffold, tools, compute, and a bounded time budget; performance is sensitive to all of these choices.
scoring: The original benchmark uses hierarchical paper-specific rubrics and an automated judge evaluated against expert grading. This Inspect port runs reproduction and grading separately: its default dummy judge returns testing zeros; substantive scoring requires the simple judge. The port excludes ungradeable children from rubric averages, reports graded_weight_fraction with score, and marks wholly ungraded samples unscored.
measures: How well an evaluated agent reproduces specified AI research outputs for the selected papers under the published PaperBench protocol.
does_not_measure: Unbounded original research ability, research taste, theory generation, lab management, reliable scientific autonomy, or acceleration of AI progress in deployment.
best_for: Comparing research-replication performance when paper set, rubric, judge, time, compute, tools, and scaffold are held fixed.
not_sufficient_for: Claims that a system can autonomously conduct general AI research or replace an end-to-end research team.
protocol_dependence: High: task instructions, paper selection, compute, time budget, scaffold, tool access, and rubric materially shape the result.
implementation_dependence: High: agent harness, environment, artifact collection, judge model and failure handling affect scores. Inspect 8-C explicitly reads paper, rubric, addenda, blacklist and submission metadata as UTF-8. The port differs from the original scaffold and its treatment of ungradeable rubric criteria.
limitations: The selected paper set is not representative of all AI research.
Rubric coverage and automated judging can miss scientifically important failure modes or reward surface reproduction.
Replication is narrower than original research and does not test agenda setting or research taste.
Results are highly sensitive to compute, time, scaffold, and tool configuration.
A dummy-judge output is a pipeline test, not evidence of research-replication capability. The pinned Inspect README reports no published results for this implementation.

Inspect excludes ungradeable criteria from the score denominator. Selective judge failures can inflate scores; graded_weight_fraction, unscored samples and error counts are needed to interpret coverage.
UTF-8 corrections can alter paper or judge inputs, or enable loading previously failing files, on hosts with another locale encoding. Numerical equivalence across versions was not tested here.
comparability: Match original benchmark and Inspect implementation versions, dataset revision, paper split, rubric, judge type and model, scoring coverage, budgets, scaffold and host text encoding. Inspect scores with ungradeable criteria are not directly comparable to published original PaperBench scores. The 7-C to 8-C encoding change does not establish empirical score equivalence.
decision_relevance: Useful for monitoring a bounded slice of AI R&D capability and designing follow-up evaluations; insufficient alone for capability thresholds or deployment decisions.

reassessment.scope: Documentary reassessment of versioned implementation, scoring and comparability. No benchmark execution, model inference, independent replication or empirical cross-version equivalence test.
